batch_strategy: family-diverse local-response, loading-contrast, and failure-repair batch

choices.reason: The m6 10/1 condition probes a high-strength donor-free heteroatom scaffold with a broad predicted finish range, testing whether late-tail behavior transfers beyond the measured difficult families.
This m101 2/1 loading condition supplies a compact, moderate-strength calibration point for a brominated carbonyl-like scaffold and helps anchor ordinary V1/V2 behavior.
The m47 2/1 condition probes a compact acceptor-rich nitrile-like scaffold at moderate loading, providing structural coverage against the late responses observed for multifunctional compounds.
This m62 1/1 PE condition tests a donor-free boronate-like environment under weak-to-moderate strength, useful as a chemically distinct ordinary control.
The m54 condition is a low-CW control with a narrow predicted regime, protecting central-distribution accuracy while difficult tail rows are sampled.

This m17 10/1 point extends strength coverage for an ester-like scaffold and can test whether its predicted shift follows the local strength response seen in the measured m208 sequence 09b5473d1d8ee26da8d, 1150272392a90f36db05, 457b3def1714039eadb3, and b66aa101a244885dd587.
The m93 10/1 PE condition gives a chemically distinct high-strength ester control for checking whether solvent-strength corrections generalize without imposing a blanket late shift.
This m4 high-strength row has a wide predicted V2 interval and tests finish-tail behavior in a halogenated polyaromatic scaffold distinct from the observed multifunctional failures.
The m149 1/1 condition supplies an intermediate-strength halogenated control, helping separate ordinary donor-free retention from late-family behavior.
This lower-strength m17 point pairs with the candidate m17 10/1 condition and tests the local onset and finish slope across strength.
The m201 0/1 condition anchors a compact halogenated nitro-like regime at weak strength, useful for controlling structural extrapolation in acceptor-rich chemistry.
This m111 20/1 point samples a high-strength ether-rich scaffold in a broad predicted regime, testing whether late V2 behavior extends to a different neutral oxygen environment.

The m103 low-volume, higher-density condition probes loading and heteroatom effects together, complementing the observed separation of onset and finish loading responses in 143bf510fe2028583763, d1172a49fca1e196a59f, and f433bc672465387d951a.
This m157 10/1 row has a wide predicted interval and tests whether a heavy halogenated aromatic remains compact or enters a genuine finish-tail regime.
The m110 10/1, 50-ul condition is a low-loading probe for a multi-ether aromatic scaffold, testing whether predicted tail width reflects loading sensitivity or structural transfer.

This m71 weak-strength donor-free control has a compact predicted onset but broad possible finish range, directly checking whether uncertainty is chemically meaningful in a simple halogenated scaffold.
The m68 20/1 point combines high CW distance with a carbonyl-rich scaffold and tests transfer from observed late families such as c4bb286978fe9078a303 and d54c93a11164b4abac6e.
This weak-strength m117 condition provides a donor-containing oxygen-rich control against the broad late m117 responses observed at higher strength and loading.
The m49 1/1 condition supplies a compact aldehyde-like control at moderate strength, helping prevent indiscriminate correction of ordinary carbonyl chemistry.
This m134 PE condition probes a compact aldehyde-like scaffold in a different solvent system and helps test transfer across mobile-phase composition.
The m156 50/1 condition samples a highly fluorinated donor-free scaffold with a broad predicted finish regime, testing whether high-strength tails generalize beyond carbonyl-rich compounds.
The m60 2/1 PE point provides a loading and solvent-system contrast to observed m60 conditions, testing whether the predicted broad interval reflects a local response rather than global uncertainty.
This m108 5/1 condition probes a brominated ether scaffold at higher strength and provides a chemically ordinary control for tail corrections.
The m186 2/1, 100-ul condition has a wide predicted V2 regime and tests finish-tail behavior in a donor-containing brominated aldehyde scaffold distinct from the measured m117 and m135 failures.
This low-strength, low-volume m112 point anchors a compact brominated ether-ester-like response and provides a loading control against the higher-width m110 rows.
The m110 1/1 condition complements the candidate m110 10/1 point, creating a local strength-response pair for onset and finish calibration.
This m74 2/1 PE condition provides a compact ester-like control at moderate strength and tests transfer across loading-solvent composition.
The m60 1/1 PE, low-volume condition complements the m60 2/1 point and helps separate solvent-strength effects from loading effects.
This m149 5/1, low-volume point creates a local strength contrast with the m149 1/1 condition and tests whether halogenated donor-free retention remains compact.
The m39 10/1 point targets a broad predicted finish regime and extends the observed m39 strength sequence, including 162ffd9b0db1fd3c1509, 3f49209a4fc102e36500, and d824f03d11ae777a2d00.
This m121 weak-strength PE condition provides a compact donor-free anisole-like control against high-width heteroatom-rich and carbonyl-rich rows.
The m184 low-volume 1/1 condition supplies a structurally simple aldehyde control and tests whether loading changes predicted finish width in an ordinary aromatic scaffold.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength response and onset/finish coupling remain scaffold-specific, with nonlinear transition locations and slopes that cannot be represented reliably by one global PE/EA trend.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched intermediate and boundary conditions can teach local transition positions and slopes, reducing inappropriate global solvent corrections for both V1 and V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do transition locations transfer within functional-group families, or remain scaffold-specific even after loading is controlled?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent conditions alter V1 and V2 differently across scaffolds, so mass alone is insufficient as a universal loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts separate onset shifts from finish-tail expansion and expose interactions with solvent strength.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and PE/EA ratio, does loading primarily shift onset, expand V2, or do both in a scaffold-dependent way?

hypotheses.content: V2 and interval width require direct local calibration; predicted quantile width is useful for finding probes but is not generally calibrated for finish-tail behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct V2 labels across compact and broad predicted regimes teach when uncertainty corresponds to a real chromatographic tail.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can structural descriptors predict finish width across families, or are local scaffold-condition anchors required?

hypotheses.content: Late-retention failures cluster across heteroatom-rich, carbonyl-rich, heteroaromatic, and multifunctional scaffolds, but their transition locations remain local.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Family-diverse difficult probes can teach transferable structural signals while preserving family-specific transition boundaries.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which local structural environments best identify a scaffold's transition into late V2 behavior?

hypotheses.content: Donor-free, halogenated, and compact acceptor-only rows are not one uniform behavior class; ordinary controls are needed alongside difficult rows to prevent indiscriminate tail correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls protect overall Row-distribution accuracy while difficult rows teach exceptions and prevent a blanket late-retention correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor-free and acceptor-only environments remain compact across strength and loading, and which are genuine exceptions?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback strengthens the local-response interpretation. The m107 sequence from 92212e7e2eb760820a7b through 60b7eed7a46a03b366b2, f96cee9775323fbf1d8b, 2cfa393cb79664e100ce, 143bf510fe2028583763, and d1172a49fca1e196a59f shows monotone onset growth but strongly nonlinear V2 expansion, with loading and strength interacting. The m177 outcomes contrast compact 61764a2e9f71f1caa18e with broad tails in 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7 and b514312eda7950cdcf1c, supporting separate onset and finish calibration. Recent m141 results, especially 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9, 6f548d72f01fc85debdc, de4e10d3a5d448ffcdda, and 434ffacb33eccce497c5, show that late onset is highly condition-local. The m13 result 1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23 was much more compact than the late 10/1 measurement c4bb286978fe9078a303, weakening any blanket V2-tail correction. I therefore increased matched boundary and loading probes while retaining neutral and molecule-novel controls.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local strength contrasts for m17, m149, m110, m39, and m208-like neighboring regimes with loading and solvent-system controls for m60, m103, m117, m112, m74, and m184. Broad predicted finish regimes in m4, m68, m71, m110, m117, m121, m156, and m186 target possible V2-tail failures directly. Donor-free, halogenated, ester-like, and compact acceptor-only rows provide ordinary controls so corrections learned from observed late families do not spill across the Row-distribution. The resulting labels should improve both condition-response representation and structural transfer while retaining coverage of the central compact regime.
